title: RWB-E8-002: the source and member names of the classification rule set, the name of the upstream reclassification event, the step name inside JOB-15, the decision reference of the record and the place the reported classification is held are not fixed by any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, RWB-E8-002 (Story, Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2, Data, Endpoints, Validation and messages); FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.10 (A2.10.1 to A2.10.4); TSD P9 Reporting v2 T3.1, T3.2, T4, T5.3, T6.1, T-A.1; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22, R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39; _work/msr/context/P9.md (ownership rows, no event and no workflow for the service)
description: The legacy story says the reported measures must follow the classification and re-ageing rules but names no rule set, no owner of the rule rows and no way for a service to read them: it lists rule_row among its data and its integration points are 'ALS and GL, Workbench'. FSD P9 A2.10 gives the feature, the rule IDs VR-P9-010-1 and BR-P9-010 and the message MSG-P1-001, and stops there. Rule R-UNI-22 names the trigger ('the account is re-aged or reclassified upstream') and no event, and R-UNI-38 names the effective date of a new rule version without saying how a reader learns of it. The service owns three tables, one read, one job, no event and no workflow, so the story must decide where a re-aged classification is held and how the rule version reaches it. This row covers those gaps once: the rule read of rwb-decision and its member names, the name and payload of the upstream reclassification fact, the step name inside JOB-15, the decision reference of the change record, the placement of the reported classification in the existing dimension columns, and the fact that no requirement row exists for the feature.
evidence: RWB-E8-002 Story: 'applies the classification and re-ageing rules and recomputes the segment when they change'; Data: 'rule_row | id, rule_id, rule_version, route_set, from_state, event_code and 9 more | DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015'; no event, no operation and no rule source named. FSD P9 A2.10.2 'Integration points: ALS and GL, Workbench'; A2.10.3.1 'VR-P9-010-1 Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status)' and 'BR-P9-010 No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version'; FSD 'Requirements served' table is empty. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22: 'the account is re-aged or reclassified upstream | Recompute the segment, re-run the gates, record the change'; R-UNI-38: 'a new rule version reaches its effective date'. TSD P9 T3.1 has dimension_code and dimension_value on measure_snapshot and no classification table; T5.3 'Events: None'. Context pack P9: tables measure_definition, measure_publish, measure_snapshot; REST GET /reports/measures; events 0; job JOB-15; workflows 0.
owner_role: rwb-reporting service owner with the rule registry owner of rwb-decision and the source-data owner of rwb-source-data
proposed: Read the classification rule rows and the rule version in force from rwb-decision on its own base as a consumed declaration with a fake and no C row; treat the upstream reclassification as an event of rwb-source-data named by the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog; run the step inside JOB-15 and inside the service's own event handler with no new workflow and no new Schedule; hold the reported classification in the existing STAGE, AGE_BAND and ROUTE rows of measure_snapshot with no new table and no new column; carry FEAT-RPT-10 as the decision reference of each change record; and confirm each element with its owner at the baseline review before the tag is raised to a signed baseline.

title: The legacy story puts the classification and re-ageing of an account in module P9 Reporting, while rule R-UNI-22 assigns the same recompute to the Workbench
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md, RWB-E8-002 (Meta: Module P9 Reporting; Story); FSD P9 Reporting v3 A2.10 and the feature table row FEAT-RPT-10; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22 and R-UNI-37; TSD P9 Reporting v2 T4 ('no case state machine of its own')
description: Two sources disagree about who owns the recompute. The story master and the FSD place the capability in module P9 Reporting and tag FEAT-RPT-10 to that module, and the service table of the target architecture keeps P9 as rwb-reporting with measure tables only. Rule R-UNI-22 of the Business Rules and Routing Logic places the same action on the Workbench, with the case owner as the actor, ALS and Workbench as the systems and one working day as the timer; R-UNI-37 does the same for an upstream correction. The reporting service cannot reopen a route or re-run a hard gate, and the case service cannot own measure definitions. The lower-precedence source is the story master, so this row records that the case-side recompute stays with rwb-case, that the reporting slice keeps the reported classification and its record, and that the two stories are joined by an event and not by a shared table. No source settles the split, so an assumption records the reading that is applied.
evidence: RWB-E8-002 Meta: 'Module | P9 Reporting', 'Feature | FEAT-RPT-10'; Story: 'recomputes the segment when they change'. FSD P9 A2.10.1 'Applies the classification and re-ageing rules and recomputes the segment when they change' with FSD owner 'Business analyst, P9'. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-22: 'Universal rules | All | ANY_ACTIVE | CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED | the account is re-aged or reclassified upstream | Recompute the segment, re-run the gates, record the change | ROUTE_D6_REOPEN | Workbench | ALS, Workbench | 1 working day'; R-UNI-37 'Recompute the segment and re-run the gates | ROUTE_D6_REOPEN | Workbench'. TSD P9 T4: 'No case state machine of its own; the module acts on events from P3 and writes through the decision log'. Target architecture slide 4 keeps P9 as rwb-reporting with the measure tables and no case state.
owner_role: rwb-reporting service owner with the rwb-case service owner and the business owner of the universal rules
proposed: Keep the case-side recompute, the route reopen and the hard-gate re-run with rwb-case under R-UNI-22 and R-UNI-37, keep the reported classification and its rule-versioned record with rwb-reporting as this story delivers, join the two by the case and rule events, and record the reading in the Change Register so the two service epics cite the same split.
